name: Strathex
description: Strathex is a classified military-tier compound developed under a Helix Biosystems defense contract that simultaneously addresses the primary physiological limitations of human combat performance: reaction time, endurance, pain threshold, and fear response, in a single tightly integrated SNT-mediated formula. It requires a compatible military-spec BCI for delivery and metabolic monitoring. The drug is not sold commercially and is not available through any legal civilian channel — possession is a criminal offense.
effects: Pain suppression comparable to surgical anesthesia in peripheral pathways
Endurance sustained at near-peak for 90 minutes
Threat identification and prioritization operating at augmented-equivalent levels
side_effects: Requires military BCI compatibility — civilian BCIs cause cascade failure
Cardiac arrest risk without medical monitoring
Psychological trauma integration impaired — PTSD profiles altered in dangerous ways
Extreme black market value makes carriers targets
cultural_context: Strathex exists in the urban mythology of the Shelf and mid-tiers as the thing that makes military operators into something other than human. Runners speak of facing Strathex-dosed soldiers with the same register they discuss fighting combat chassis — as something categorically different. Black market doses circulate rarely and expensively, often pulled from dead soldiers. The Helix defense division denies the specific formula and the name. Among Tier 4-5 security professionals who know it's real, possession of a single dose represents both an extraordinary capability and an extraordinary risk.
story_hooks: A Shelf runner acquires a dose of Strathex from a dead soldier's kit and doesn't know what it is — they just know the soldier was frightening and this was in his chest pocket
Helix's military contract division has lost a shipment of Strathex — six doses unaccounted for — and is running a covert recovery operation that looks, from the outside, like a series of murders

A crew is hired to hit a target who they're told is corporate security; they arrive to find someone dosed with Strathex, and now they need to survive long enough to understand why someone burned a military-grade asset on what looked like a routine job
